A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same synthetic-family knowledge study, with matching experiments and Appendices A–D. Text, equations, figures, and relocated appendix material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original transformer-training, representation-probing, relational-algebra, and model-editing results in Figures 2–11 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and expands the probe sample-size experiments in Appendix D.2.1 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: The GPT-NeoX architecture, three probing procedures, RESCAL ridge objective and SVD solution, and layer-wise MLP fine-tuning editor remain unchanged. Additional sample-size experiments test the existing procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,000-family synthetic dataset, eight relations, withheld father/mother prediction tasks, and single-fact editing scenarios. Changing probe sample counts does not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix Figure 7 expands from a linear-probe-only sample-size diagnostic to a comparison of linear and bilinear probes at matched sample counts. The main comparison among linear, translational, and bilinear probes in Figure 3 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2.1 extends linear probing from n=10 and 100 to include n=500 and adds bilinear evaluations at all three sample counts. The main training budgets, dataset splits, model configuration, and editing protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing probe sample-size sensitivity analysis is extended to test whether substantially more data rescues linear probing and how limited data affects bilinear probing. Figure 7 adds evidence of bilinear underfitting at small sample counts; other supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three training seeds per weight-decay setting and averages over 50 independent edits. Shaded uncertainty displays already existed; the expanded Figure 7 introduces no stated new uncertainty-estimation procedure, run count, or significance test.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds linear n=500 results and bilinear sample-size curves, with non-cursed bilinear accuracy peaking around 0.84 at n=500. The retained linear n=10 and 100 curves also change, but unexplained aggregation differences prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance changes. Other plotted results, including R-squared=0.939 in Figure 5, are retained.

T1.justification: The probe definitions, objectives, inversion/composition operations, and Appendix C derivation remain mathematically unchanged. The new attention-head discussion offers a hypothesis rather than a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the previously unexplored question from representational geometry generally to the specific algebraic mechanism supporting reasoning. The first-systematic-analysis novelty claim is also softened. The central claims connecting bilinear representations, reversal inference, and editing generalization remain.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds a specific attention-head mechanism hypothesis and explicitly qualifies that bilinear structure alone is insufficient unless editing preserves it. It removes the substantive catastrophic-generalization discussion about unintended propagation. These revisions materially change the mechanism explanation and applicability boundaries; the synthetic-data limitation remains.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly links the retained n=10 choice to a sweep over 10, 100, and 500, while Appendix D.2.1 clarifies that n denotes training samples per relation. Architecture, implementation, hardware, data-generation instructions, and editing details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gurnee and Tegmark, Engels et al., Nishi et al., Elhelo and Geva, and Zitong Yang et al., connecting the study to geometric representations, representation shattering, attention heads, and synthetic pretraining. It qualifies the novelty positioning. The Sohee Yang preprint-to-publication update retains the same cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, contribution bullets gain descriptive labels, and the discussion is reordered and substantially revised. Terminology and prose are edited throughout, alongside title, affiliation, and publication-header changes. This is extensive narrative editing despite stable methods.

P2.justification: Figure 7 changes from two linear-probe panels to six linear/bilinear panels, with revised axes, styling, and caption. Main figure captions are rewritten, and appendix figures are regrouped across pages. The graphical content of Figures 1–6 and 8–11 is retained.

improvement.justification: Extending the existing sample-size check to n=500 and bilinear probes modestly strengthens robustness evidence. More qualified novelty positioning and the requirement to preserve geometry improve interpretation. The gain is limited by unexplained revisions to existing Figure 7 linear curves and removal of the useful unintended-propagation discussion; the core evidence and synthetic-only scope remain unchanged.
